segments.text: He started caring for his father at 24 and once broke down
I felt resentful at first. Why me?
He suffered three strokes in two years
I was attending classes then
It was really stressful
He had to carry his crying child into the operating theatre
I had to carry him into the operating theatre.
I was...
He kept screaming in fear
That was how I carried him into the operating theatre
Daughters shouldn’t be the only caregivers for parents
Gender doesn’t matter when caring for parents
It’s your responsibility
To have more time to supervise her diet
I quit my job
Losing weight from caregiving responsibilities
You’re all very skinny
My mom always says
You don’t seem to gain weight no matter what you eat
It’s been ten years and I still look the same
When a family member requires long-term care
who should take on the duty of caregiving?
In the past, we used to think
as men, we are usually the breadwinners
Caregiving duties, especially for our parents
seldom fall on our shoulders
But in the recent years
this mindset has been slowly shifting in Singapore
More men are becoming caregivers
Let’s introduce our three guests today

Lim Eng Tiong (62)
Quit his job and has been caring for his mother for four years

Eric Lim (37)
Balanced his studies while caring for his sick father for six years

Phua Wee Seng (52)
Ended his business and has been caring for his sick son for 12 years
Let’s start with Eng Tiong
At 58, you resigned from your job at the electronics factory
When did you first decide to resign?
I’m living with my 90-year-old mother now
A few years ago, because of diabetes
she developed a bacterial infection
and was admitted into ICU
She recovered miraculously
It was then that I realised
the importance of monitoring her condition
to prevent this from happening again
To have more time to supervise her diet
I quit my job
How about you, Wee Seng?
Before my son turned six
he was a normal, lively boy
He fell sick at six years old
I resigned from my job then
and started my own business
for a more flexible working arrangement
to stay close to my children
When he fell sick
I felt this was what I had to do as his father
I have two other kids
I want to be a good role model for them too
If I don’t care for my child
what kind of message am I giving them?
That was a key teaching moment
How about you, Eric?
You started caring for your father at 24
while still studying

Yes, it was October 2013
I still remember clearly
I was on campus when my mom called
Come home now
Your dad fainted at the void deck
He hit his head and was bleeding
We brought him to the hospital
That’s when we found out he had suffered a stroke
How did you come to your decision
when you were still studying?
It was the decision that made the most sense
I have two older brothers who are teachers
So they had to go to school in the mornings
I had more time compared to them
I’d attend classes in the morning
and bring my dad for physiotherapy in the afternoon
As a student, I didn’t have income
My brothers paid for everything
My wife took a year of unpaid leave
But seeing our son in his condition
broke her heart
It was very hard for her to accept
After six months
I told her to return to work
At least, you’ll have colleagues-
to talk to
Yes, to confide in
You won’t feel so helpless everyday
Our son couldn’t talk to us
He had to be fed through a tube
He needed diapers, the diapers had to be changed
She was under a lot of mental stress then
How about Eric? Your father suffered a stroke
and passed away after six years
How did you manage to get through it?
It was tough
He had three strokes in two years
To me, it was particularly tough
because he developed vascular dementia
He had mood swings and was more irritable
He couldn’t sleep at night
He slept fine in the morning, but not at night
I became moody too from the lack of sleep
I still had classes to attend
After that, I had to work
It was really stressful for me
For me, the work doesn’t stop at night too
He needs to pee
So, I’ll have to change his diapers
Not getting enough sleep is the norm
It’s the norm
How do we balance between rest and caregiving?
Honestly, it’s not easy
It’s not easy at all
Why do I say that?
Is that why you’re so skinny?
Yes
You’re all very skinny
My mom often said
You don’t seem to gain weight no matter what you eat
It’s been ten years and I still look the same
Like Eric said, we’ll feel stressed sometimes
We need to talk to someone
Meet some friends and confide in them
Share your challenges with them
It will help in some ways
Do you ever feel conflicted?
No
Gender doesn’t matter when caring for parents
It’s your responsibility
In traditional Chinese culture
filial piety is a virtue
Our parents raised us
We have a duty
to care for them when they are old and vulnerable
That is our responsibility
I felt resentful at first. Why me?
I had a long life ahead of me
I was only 24 then
I thought, if I could travel with my friends
wouldn’t it be great?
But when my dad suffered a stroke
my university offered me an opportunity
to study in the US for six months
I didn’t know if I could afford it
When I told my dad
he didn’t hesitate at all
He asked if I was free the next day?
Let’s go to the bank
He withdrew a sum of money and told me
Don’t worry. Just pursue your dreams
When I found out my dad had a stroke
I knew in my heart
I had to take care of him
How about you, Wee Seng?
Any unforgettable moments for you?
After getting the diagnosis, he was admitted to the hospital
He had a stem cell transplant
He needed chemotherapy
I donated my stem cells
for the stem cell transplant
We had to stay in the ICU for two months
When he was admitted, he could still talk
But he couldn’t walk properly
He had to undergo a lot of preparation
before the chemotherapy
I remember he was very scared
He didn’t want to do the surgery
My wife couldn’t do anything
I had to carry him into the operating theatre
I was...
I was...
He kept crying and kicking
screaming in fear
That was how I carried him into the operating theatre
We can get stressed too
We also have to deal with many problems
especially when it comes to communication
The old folks like to eat certain food
If you tell my mother
You can’t eat this, you can’t eat that
She’ll get upset because she can’t eat anything
Sometimes, she’ll buy food made with flour for herself
She doesn’t understand the severity of the situation
I need to explain things to her patiently
For most families, we don’t talk about it
Sometimes, there is an unspoken understanding
Those who have more time should do more
Sometimes, that can be your female family members
Sometimes, it’s those who are single and unmarried
Eng Tiong, you’re single, right?
Yes
I think that if you’re living with your mother
it’s your responsibility to take care of her
ensure she is healthy and eats right
My siblings do their part too
They will visit my mother
That’s important too
It’s important for her mental wellbeing
It helps her keep a positive mindset
They’re willing to hire a domestic helper
Everyone chips in
There’s a common misconception
that when a family member is sick
you only need one caregiver to care for them
But one person is not enough
Because we’re not robots
We need to eat, go to the toilet
and take breaks
Usually, you need at least two people
You need a team to care for one person
When you said that, they kept nodding
I agree
It’s important to have another person
who can share the load
Yes. When I first started caring for my dad
I didn’t want to ask for help
Not from my family, friends, colleagues or my boss
Later, I realised
asking for help is a form of strength too
I remember one time
they asked me out for dinner
I told them I had to care for my dad
because his condition was unstable
They said, it’s okay, Eric
We can have dinner near your place
I was so shocked
By how understanding they were
Wee Seng, you used to be in the baking business
Did your decision mean you had to close your business?
Yes, trying to run a business
while there is so much uncertainty at home
would be unsustainable
I still believe that I made the right decision
If I hadn’t done that
we might have faced bigger problems down the road
Eng Tiong, you could have continued working
When you made the decision to resign
did you feel conflicted?
Not really
I’ve had that job for over 20 years
You must have financial planning
That’s very important
When it comes to the subject
of men leaving the workforce
people have different views
Luckily, my family and friends support me
They’ll ask me if I’m coping well
especially financially
Sometimes, they’ll help out as well
I can tell that they care
If you are to look back now
what experience do you think changed you the most?
I used to see it as a sacrifice
I was young then
I had so many things I wanted to do
I was only in my twenties
But now, I don’t see it as a sacrifice
During the six years of caring for my dad
I learned a lot from him
Near the end, he couldn’t talk
But through his eyes alone, he taught me so much
Your mother’s fallen ill now
Do you find any difference
between caring for her and your father?
When I was caring for my dad
I was still very young
I got lost in my thoughts and got distracted easily
I might use my phone
But now, when I’m with my mom
when I bring her to the hospital for consultation
I’m focused only on her
She has my full attention
We must cherish what we have
Because it’s too late to regret when you lose them
Most importantly, just do your best
Don’t worry about what’s going to happen in the future
As long as you stay positive
you can handle whatever problems that come your way
We may not be able to solve everything ourselves
But we have family and friends
My son taught me so much more
He taught me many life lessons
After he developed his condition
he was like a baby again
He needed diapers
I had to get to know him all over again
I had to discover what makes him uncomfortable
and how to care for him better
I needed more patience in everything
That was what he taught me and my family
How would you describe your decision in a few words?
Wee Seng?
It’s an expression of love
and a father’s duty
If I had to choose again
I’d still do the same without hesitation
How about you, Eric?
Same.
I don’t regret my decision to care for my dad
He has made me stronger, braver and more mature
He also inspired me
The work I’m doing now
to help people improve the quality of their sleep
I don’t regret my decision.
It’s the right one
The key is your impetus
To me, it’s to ensure my mother is well taken care of
We are often caught in the middle
of caring for our parents and children
We can’t leave our parents,
but we can’t neglect our children either
If it were you
what will you choose?
Leave your comments below
Thank you for your time
